about: Unicode text -> Shree-Lipi 7 Telugu bytes (fonts SHREE-TEL7-Apoorva-0900 M0900890/N0902890.TTF, SHREE-TEL7-Asmitha-1642 M1642890/N1644890.TTF, Shree-Tel7-001/002 WTEL7001/2.TTF; the 4/5/6 fonts SHREE-TEL-Apoorva/Asmitha M09000F0/N09020F0/M16420F0/N16440F0.TTF have the same code set and identical glyphs), answered by Shree's own composers S8TelU64.dll (TutorGetMappedCodeW, Unicode) and S8Tel764.dll (TutorGetMappedCode, raw bytes) for the same keystroke. bytes = the 7 composer's raw output, one hex byte per glyph code (bytes 80-9F are raw bytes: in a document they sit on their Windows-1252 code points, except 90 which the fonts map at U+0090). Every probe set and every vendor keyboard was captured twice in separate processes: identical (the only difference is the random unit count the 7 composer returns for "no answer"). kind: vendor-key = a key (layer 0, Ctrl+Space, or the composer raw code layer) of one of the 16 shipped .TEL keyboards loaded from its ORIGINAL path (the composers switch typing mode by name: ENG/PHONETIC answer a consonant with its virama form; a vowel-sign key alone types the independent vowel); source names the keyboard, key and codes. canonical = probe in Shree's typing order for Telugu: the consonant (which the 7 composer writes with its talakattu, క = 4D E6 FC), then the vowel sign (which replaces the talakattu: కి = 4D EC FC, కా = 4D 3E), then ం ః ఁ; the ra-vattu ్ర is the code D7 struck BEFORE the letter it belongs to (the vendor charts' order: TYPEWRIT K = D7 first, ITR Ctrl+Space g first, INDICA/APPLE slots D7 + C), and the 7 composer writes its hook BEFORE the letter (క్ర = 7B 4D E6 FC, క్రి = 7B 4D EC FC; 5B before a letter with ై: క్రై = 5B 4D F0 FC 4F; on త/ట after a link the combined glyphs 88/89: స్త్ర = E7 DC 88, ష్ట్ర = E7 D9 89; శ్రీ = 7D) - the same place the శ్రీ ligature 7D draws it; conjuncts through the link code 64 (C1 + the subjoined form of C2, క్క = 4D E6 FC 50; a vowel sign on the cluster changes C1: క్కి = 4D EC FC 50); ై = the e-shape of the letter + 4F (కై = 4D F0 FC 4F; on a cluster typed ై first: క్కై = 4D F0 FC 4F 50); canonical:halant = code 44 (Unicode virama + ZWNJ: the visible virama glyph, క్‌ = 4D 8A FC); canonical:ra-vattu ED = always the second hook 5B (accepted, ranked after D7). The Unicode composer writes the ra-vattu as "*్ర" where it was struck and leaves it for the NEXT consonant (క + D7 + క = "క*్రక" = కక్ర; the 7 composer writes 4D E6 FC 7B 4D E6 FC, the hook before the second క); uComposer keeps that raw answer, unicode is it read as ్ర behind the cluster that follows. preferred: vendor key, then canonical other than ED, then fewer bytes (క్ష: the code 5E = 84 E6 FC, C + link + ష = 4D E6 FC DB; both accepted), then more probes; accepted keeps every canonical spelling. alt:* = the composer answer for another typing order (the pending ra-vattu: D7 struck after a letter with no letter after it, the hook written AFTER the letter, C 7B - visually on the wrong side, and a sign struck after it is dropped; a sign struck before the link: same bytes except ృ) - kept, not used as truth. quirk:* = the Unicode composer wrote something other than the codes mean (it drops క్ష after the link and a tail after a lone sign, and drops ZWJ/ZWNJ after the link), or the 7 composer dropped a code the Unicode composer wrote (the pending virama, ర after the link, a vowel sign struck after the ra-vattu, ౄ on a letter, ఌ ౡ ౣ ॥ ₹ × ÷ [ ]), a code only the 7 composer types (E1 -> 93 and 86 DB E7 E9 EA EB EE), or a lone vowel sign (7 carrier E6 61 E6 61) - kept for evidence, not used. Unicode keys are what the Unicode composer wrote (ై filed as U+0C48; ె + ౖ is joined to it). Rules with examples: tel7-patterns.txt. Strings a table needs that the composer never spells directly: tel7-composer-gaps.json (derived, not truth).

fontCheck.method: fonts/family-check.json (fontcmp.js + ttf.js): (3,1) cmap of every installed Telugu Shree face - 7: WTEL7001.TTF (Shree-Tel7-001), WTEL7002.TTF (Shree-Tel7-002), WTEL701T/702T.TTF (7-code "T" faces), M0900890/N0902890.TTF (SHREE-TEL7-Apoorva-0900 regular/bold), M1642890/N1644890.TTF (SHREE-TEL7-Asmitha-1642 regular/bold); 4/5/6: M09000F0/N09020F0.TTF (SHREE-TEL-Apoorva-0900), M16420F0/N16440F0.TTF (SHREE-TEL-Asmitha-1642). Per code: glyph id, advance, sha1 of the glyf bytes.
fontCheck.sameGlyph: Codes that draw the identical outline with the identical advance (fonts/same-glyph-codes.json): 7B = 93 and 90 = A0 in every face (93 is the glyph of the 7-only code E1, so a 93 ra-vattu looks exactly like the 7B Shree writes); B6 = E6 in the Apoorva faces only.
fontCheck.composerBytesThatDrawTheWrongGlyph: ః = 40 and ఁ = B6 (both talakattu ticks in every face; the visarga glyph is 5D, the candrabindu glyph 97): see tel7-groundtruth-glyphfix.json
fontCheck.result: All ten full faces have the same 216 codes on the same code points with the same glyph ids. The same design in the two families is identical code by code (outline bytes and advance): M0900890 = M09000F0, N0902890 = N09020F0, M1642890 = M16420F0, N1644890 = N16440F0 (216/216 each). Shree-Tel7-001/002 have no 4/5/6 twin (other designs, same code set and glyph ids). Bytes 80 81 8D 8E 8F 9D 9E have no glyph in any face; 90 sits on U+0090, every other byte 80-9F on its Windows-1252 code point. ONE table serves both families.

counts.notProbed: A conjunct slot holds at most 4 codes and a slot reference inside a slot is ignored (shown on Punjabi this round), so these are not in the truth: three-consonant clusters C1్C2్C3 (5 codes: C link C link C) other than C1్C2్ర (C link C D7) and క్ష + ్C; C1్C2 + sign + tail; C1్C2 + ై + tail; C1్C2్ర + a sign; ై + tail on a cluster. The probes with ై or the halant 44 at the end needed a space after them (the 7 composer leaves ై/44 pending), so those rows had one code fewer to spend.
